subject: On‑prem visibility consolidation: SIEM adapter and trace hook review
messages:

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability handoff for on‑prem deploy — SIEM adapter questions

Hi Hiro / team,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. As we start the security review with our on‑prem team, a few concrete questions came up about how Redwood will deliver observability out of our VPC appliance:

- SIEM: we need to confirm supported protocols and the delivery model. Will you provide a push adapter (syslog/HEC) from the forwarder, or do you expect us to pull? What auth patterns do you support (mTLS, HEC token)?
- Trace hooks: we run a filtered sampled tracing approach; we need < 1% overhead at 95th p50. Can you provide minimal patch points and the expected span attributes we can rely on?
- Data residency & evidence: our audit needs an evidence bundle (logs+hashes + timestamps) at weekly cadence. Can Redwood sign/export that, or do we need to implement a local collector?

I've looped in security@acmeanalytics.com. Can we get a short technical note and a sample spec by EOD Monday? We also want a short checklist for our ops team to validate the forwarder.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Connors
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer — Acme Analytics

P.S. attaching the partial compliance checklist — see attachment: acme-sample-checklist.xlsx (we'll share the full doc in Drive)

From: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff for on‑prem deploy — SIEM adapter questions

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and a spec draft attached.

- SIEM delivery: Redwood provides a push model from the local forwarder. Supported targets: syslog (RFC5424), Splunk HEC, and S3 for archive. We support HEC tokens + optional mTLS for mutual auth toward collector endpoints.
- Trace hooks: we expose lightweight OpenTelemetry-compatible hooks; default sampling is adaptive, but you can pin sample rate on ingress. Overhead is typically under 0.6% P95 in our benchmarks when only span headers are emitted.
- Evidence bundles: we can generate signed weekly evidence packages (SHA256 manifests + timestamping) and store them in a customer‑owned S3 / SMB location. We can also push hashes to a customer audit endpoint if required.

Attached: redwood-siem-adapter-spec-v1.pdf (draft) and trace-hook-snippets-v0.3.zip — both are drafts but should give your ops team a concrete checklist.

Expanded notes (ops checklist highlights):
1) Network: allow outbound TCP to your collector on ports 514 (syslog), 8088/443 for HEC. If using mTLS, we'll need CA certs.
2) Auth: HEC token for Splunk is simplest; for mTLS we provide a client cert rotation tool that integrates with your KMS.
3) Schema & mapping: logs will be JSON lines by default; we include a "redwood_source" field and trace_id/span_id when available for cross‑referencing.
4) Sampling: trace hook can be configured to attach minimal context to logs without full span emission.
5) Evidence: we will produce a signed manifest and give instructions to validate chain-of-custody.

Action items:
- We'll push the full spec and quick validation script to your Drive link by Monday morning.
- Can we lock a 60‑minute technical runbook session with your ops on Tuesday 9/16? Ben, Kimberly, Marissa — can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-siem-adapter-spec-v1.pdf, trace-hook-snippets-v0.3.zip

Subject: Re: Observability handoff for on‑prem deploy — SIEM adapter questions

Thanks Sarah — a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Trace hook implementation: we embed a tiny OTel shim in the inference host. It exports span_id & trace_id into the log envelope as headers: redwood.trace_id, redwood.span_id, redwood.sampled. We deliberately keep payload minimal (headers only) unless "full_traces" is enabled in the local config.
- Performance: our internal perf runs (gpt-2 small workloads) show median CPU overhead <0.2% and P95 <0.7% with header emission only. If Acme wants absolute worstcase guarantees we can ship a micro‑benchmark script for their baseline.
- Backpressure & buffering: forwarder uses a disk‑backed ring buffer; in heavy egress scenarios we switch to compressed JSON batches and degrade sampling first.

I attached trace-hook-snippets-v0.3.zip with example config blocks and a lightweight microbenchmark tool.

Kimberly Park
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hiro / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turn. That helps. A few followups from our security team:

- mTLS: we prefer mTLS for the HEC endpoint. Can Redwood accept rotating client certs issued by our internal CA, or do you require a public CA for certs?
- Evidence signing: if Redwood produces signed manifests, will the private key stay on the appliance (customer‑managed) or will Redwood retain keys? We need keys to be customer‑managed for audit.
- Data retention: logs older than 90 days must be purged from any transit buffers; can you confirm the forwarder enforces this?

Also — can your team share a lightweight acceptance checklist we can run during our staging cutover? If you can include the network ACLs and a short splunk mapping stanza example that would be perfect.

Best,
Sarah

Sarah — quick replies and a proposed acceptance checklist (summary below). We'll also add the full checklist to the Drive link.

- mTLS & certs: we support customer‑managed certs. The appliance accepts client certs signed by your internal CA; the private key for the evidence signatures will remain on the customer side if you choose that option. We'll provide an integration guide for key rotation tied to your KMS.
- Retention: the forwarder enforces TTL on the local disk ring buffer; older files are deleted after the configured retention window. Default we set to 14 days for staging, can be tuned to 90 for production.

Proposed short acceptance checklist (summary):
1) Network: allow outbound 8088/443 to Splunk HEC and 514 for syslog; ensure egress TLS inspection is disabled or whitelisted for HEC endpoint.
2) Auth: validate mTLS handshake using customer CA certs (we include a verification script).
3) Payload: validate presence of redwood.trace_id/redwood.span_id headers in logs for a set of sample traces (script provided).
4) Performance: run microbenchmark; validate P95 CPU overhead <1% for your steady state.
5) Retention & evidence: trigger evidence generation and validate manifest signatures + file retention purge.

Ben — let's lock the Tuesday runbook with Acme and include Splunk sales for the HEC mapping examples; do you have availability to lead the mapping session?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
